traps.title: UPSC Exam Traps & Pitfalls
items: Trap 1: The Capital Transfer: Do not confuse Afonso de Albuquerque with Nino da Cunha. Albuquerque conquered Goa in 1510, but it was Nino da Cunha who officially shifted the capital of the Portuguese Empire from Cochin to Goa in 1530.
Trap 2: Predecessor Chronology: Ensure you know that Nino da Cunha succeeded Lopo Vaz de Sampaio (who was sent back to Lisbon in chains), and was succeeded by Garcia de Noronha in 1538.

Trap 3: Bengal Port Names: Do not swap Porto Grande and Porto Pequeno. Porto Grande refers to Chittagong, while Porto Pequeno refers to Hooghly. Both were established in Bengal under Nino da Cunha's tenure in 1536.

sections.title: 1. Transfer of the Capital from Cochin to Goa (1530)
sections.content:
Background of the Shift: Nino da Cunha assumed office as Governor of Portuguese India in November 1529, succeeding Lopo Vaz de Sampaio. His first major administrative reform was the official transfer of the capital of the Estado da Índia from Cochin to Goa in 1530. While Cochin had served as the early headquarters since 1505, it was geographically peripheral and politically dependent on the local Raja of Cochin, whose domestic court often clashed with Portuguese commercial interests.

Strategic and Economic Rationale: Goa, conquered by Afonso de Albuquerque in 1510, offered superior natural advantages. It possessed a highly defensible island geography flanked by the Mandovi and Zuari rivers, active shipyards for vessel maintenance, and a centralized location on the western Konkan coast. Furthermore, Goa was the primary hub for the lucrative Arabian horse trade with the Deccan kingdoms. By establishing Goa as the metropolitan center, the Portuguese secured sovereign, independent administrative control, housing the Governor's residence, the High Court (Relação), and the Royal Treasury (Chancelaria) under direct Crown rule.

masteryZone.q: Who was the predecessor of Nino da Cunha from whom he took over the governorship in 1529?
masteryZone.sol: Nino da Cunha succeeded Lopo Vaz de Sampaio in November 1529.

masteryZone.q: In which year did Nino da Cunha officially transfer the capital of the Portuguese State of India from Cochin to Goa?
masteryZone.sol: The capital was officially shifted to Goa in 1530 CE.

masteryZone.q: What major geographical advantage did Goa have over Cochin that motivated Nino da Cunha's capital transfer?
masteryZone.sol: Goa possessed a highly central Konkan position and an excellent natural deep-water harbor.

masteryZone.q: Which Indian state entity did the Portuguese depend on politically while their capital was in Cochin?
masteryZone.sol: The Portuguese base in Cochin was dependent on and leased from the local Raja of Cochin.

masteryZone.q: Who originally conquered Goa in 1510, which later became the capital under Nino da Cunha?
masteryZone.sol: Afonso de Albuquerque conquered Goa from Bijapur in 1510.

masteryZone.q: What administrative infrastructure in Goa made it ideal for the new metropolitan headquarters of the Estado da Índia?
opts: Excellent shipbuilding yards and defensive river systems
masteryZone.sol: Goa had active shipbuilding yards and was flanked naturally by Mandovi and Zuari rivers.

masteryZone.q: Under whose governorship did Cochin first serve as the de facto headquarters of the Portuguese?
masteryZone.sol: Francisco de Almeida established Cochin as the de facto capital starting in 1505.

masteryZone.q: In which month and year did Nino da Cunha arrive in India to assume his duties?
masteryZone.sol: Nino da Cunha assumed office in November 1529.

masteryZone.q: What was the name of the Portuguese administrative and colonial state entity in Asia?
masteryZone.sol: The official administrative name was the Estado da Índia (State of India).

masteryZone.q: Which Deccan state had the Portuguese wrested Goa from in 1510?
masteryZone.sol: Goa was conquered from the Bijapur Sultanate in 1510.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following factors influenced the decision to shift the capital to Goa? (Select all that apply)
opts: Goa's centralized position on the western coast
Desire to escape political dependence on the Cochin Raja
Direct request by the Mughal Emperor
masteryZone.sol: Goa's harbor, position, and independence from Cochin were key. Mughals were not involved in this decision.

masteryZone.q: Select the properties of Goa that made it an ideal naval base for the Portuguese. (Select all that apply)
opts: Natural defensive river systems (Mandovi and Zuari)
A central hub for the Arabian horse trade
Large diamond mines in the immediate vicinity
masteryZone.sol: River defense, shipyards, and horse trade made Goa highly valuable. It did not have local diamond mines.

masteryZone.q: Which challenges did Cochin present as a capital before 1530? (Select all that apply)
opts: Geographically peripheral location in the far south
Encroachment of British East India Company forces
masteryZone.sol: Cochin was peripheral, threatened by Calicut, and had limited space. The British were not present in 1530.

masteryZone.q: What offices were relocated from Cochin to Goa during the 1530 transfer? (Select all that apply)
opts: The Board of Directors of the Dutch VOC
masteryZone.sol: The Governor's office, court, and treasury shifted. The Dutch VOC did not exist in 1530.

masteryZone.q: Identify the key predecessors who governed Portuguese India before Nino da Cunha. (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Almeida, Albuquerque, and Sampaio governed before him. Garcia de Noronha succeeded him in 1538.

masteryZone.q: Select the benefits that the Portuguese secured by establishing Goa as their metropolitan center. (Select all that apply)
opts: Enhanced prestige among Indian regional powers
Direct control over Deccan trade routes
Secure base for building larger naval vessels
masteryZone.sol: Prestige, trade control, and ship-building were key benefits. It did not isolate them.

masteryZone.q: Which rivers flank the island of Goa, providing it with natural defenses? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Goa is situated on an island flanked by the Mandovi and Zuari rivers.

masteryZone.q: Which statements are correct regarding the administrative transition of 1530? (Select all that apply)
opts: It was executed smoothly without major military conflicts
It marked the maturity of the Estado da Índia
It immediately led to the capture of Madras
It was planned and authorized by Lisbon
masteryZone.sol: The transfer was smooth, authorized by Lisbon, and marked administrative maturity. Madras expansion occurred later.

masteryZone.q: Identify the strategic imports that passed through Goa in the 1530s. (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Goa handled horses, silks, regional spices, and Chinese porcelain imports.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following local groups in Goa interacted with Nino da Cunha's administration? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Saraswat Brahmins, merchant guilds, and Gauncars interacted with the administration. Mughals had no presence in Goa.

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha was the first Governor to govern from Goa as the official capital.
masteryZone.sol: He transferred the capital to Goa in 1530, becoming the first to officially reside there as capital.

masteryZone.q: Cochin remained the capital of the Portuguese Empire in the East until 1550.
masteryZone.sol: It was transferred in 1530.

masteryZone.q: Lopo Vaz de Sampaio handed over power to Nino da Cunha peacefully without any court disputes in Lisbon.
masteryZone.sol: Sampaio was arrested and sent back to Lisbon in chains due to administrative disputes.

masteryZone.q: Goa was located further north than Cochin, placing it closer to the Gujarat and Deccan conflicts.
masteryZone.sol: Goa's northern position allowed better monitoring of Gujarat and Deccan kingdoms.

masteryZone.q: The Transfer of Capital in 1530 required a royal decree from King John III of Portugal.
masteryZone.sol: Imperial administrative changes of this scale were authorized and approved by the Portuguese King (John III).

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha died in Goa and was buried in the Basilica of Bom Jesus.
masteryZone.sol: He died at sea during his return voyage to Portugal.

masteryZone.q: The Raja of Cochin was relieved when the Portuguese shifted their main capital to Goa.
masteryZone.sol: It reduced the direct Portuguese military dominance over his domestic court at Cochin.

masteryZone.q: The shipyards of Goa were incapable of building large ships, forcing the Portuguese to import all vessels.
masteryZone.sol: Goa's shipyards were famous for building sturdy teakwood vessels.

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha arrived in India in the year 1535.
masteryZone.sol: He arrived in November 1529.

masteryZone.q: The transfer of the capital from Cochin to Goa had no impact on naval administration.
masteryZone.sol: It centralized and greatly improved the coordination of Portuguese naval patrol fleets.

masteryZone.q: Goa was completely landlocked, requiring the Portuguese to build canals to the sea.
masteryZone.sol: Goa is a coastal island with excellent river estuaries and direct sea access.

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha was the second Viceroy of Portuguese India.
masteryZone.sol: He was a Governor, not a Viceroy, and Francisco de Almeida was the first Viceroy.

masteryZone.sol: He succeeded Lopo Vaz de Sampaio.

masteryZone.sol: The capital transfer occurred in 1530 CE.

masteryZone.sol: Cochin served as the early capital from 1505 to 1530.

masteryZone.sol: King John III succeeded King Manuel I and authorized the transfer.

masteryZone.sol: The Mandovi and Zuari rivers form the island of Goa.

masteryZone.sol: Goa was the main hub for importing war horses for Deccan kingdoms.

masteryZone.q: The Portuguese shipyards in Goa utilized local __________ wood to build vessels.
masteryZone.sol: Sturdy local teakwood was used for shipbuilding.

masteryZone.sol: Almeida ruled from Cochin as Viceroy, Sampaio was at Cochin, and da Cunha shifted it to Goa.

masteryZone.q: Match the geographical entities of Goa with their description:
masteryZone.sol: Mandovi is the northern river, Zuari the southern river, and Timoja was the Hindu privateer.

options.text: Arrival of da Cunha in India
Recall of da Cunha to Lisbon

masteryZone.sol: 1529 was arrival, 1530 was capital transfer, and 1538 was his recall.

masteryZone.q: Match the historical roles with their respective holders in 1529-1530:
masteryZone.sol: Da Cunha was incoming, Sampaio deposed, and John III the King.

masteryZone.q: Match the early Portuguese factories with their regions:
masteryZone.sol: Cochin is south Malabar, Cannanore is north Malabar, Goa is Konkan.

masteryZone.q: Match the administrative titles with their functions in the Estado da Índia:
masteryZone.sol: Governador is chief executive, Feitor is factor/agent, Ouvidor is judge.

masteryZone.q: What is the name of the river that flows north of the island of Goa?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: Mandovi River. Explanation: The Mandovi River bounds Goa to the north.

masteryZone.q: Who was the King of Portugal when the capital was transferred to Goa?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: King John III. Explanation: King John III authorized the transfer of the capital in 1530.

masteryZone.q: Which city served as the Portuguese capital before Goa?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: Cochin. Explanation: Cochin was the capital from the establishment of the Viceroyalty in 1505 until 1530.

masteryZone.q: Who was arrested by Nino da Cunha upon his arrival in India in 1529?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: Lopo Vaz de Sampaio. Explanation: Nino da Cunha arrested Sampaio for administrative offenses and sent him to Lisbon.

masteryZone.q: Why was Cochin abandoned as the primary capital?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: It was geographically peripheral and politically dependent on the local Raja. Explanation: Goa offered better independence and central location.

masteryZone.q: In which region of India is Goa situated?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: The Konkan Coast. Explanation: Goa is strategically located along the central Konkan coast of western India.

masteryZone.q:

sections.title: 2. Negotiations and Acquisition of Bassein (1534)
sections.content:
The Mughal Threat to Gujarat: By 1534, the Sultan of Gujarat, Bahadur Shah, was facing a catastrophic military invasion from the Mughal Emperor Humayun, who had captured Mandu and Ahmedabad. Desperate for allies and military assistance, Bahadur Shah turned to Governor Nino da Cunha for aid. To secure a Portuguese alliance and naval gunners, the Sultan signed the Treaty of Bassein on December 23, 1534.

Cession of Bassein, Salsette, and Bombay: Under the Treaty of Bassein, the Gujarat Sultanate ceded the strategic province of Bassein (Baçaim), the island of Salsette, and the seven islands of Bombay (Bombaim) to the Portuguese Crown. Additionally, the treaty imposed strict maritime regulations: Gujarat's merchant vessels were forced to route through Portuguese customs houses, pay duties, and obtain Cartazes (navigation licenses). The Sultan was also prohibited from constructing warships without Portuguese consent, effectively demilitarizing Gujarat's naval capacity in exchange for military backing against Humayun.

masteryZone.q: Which Sultan of Gujarat ceded Bassein to Nino da Cunha under the Treaty of Bassein?
masteryZone.sol: Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat ceded Bassein due to the Mughal invasion.

masteryZone.q: Which Mughal Emperor was invading Gujarat in 1534, forcing Bahadur Shah to ally with the Portuguese?
masteryZone.sol: Mughal Emperor Humayun was invading Gujarat in 1534.

masteryZone.q: On what exact date was the historic Treaty of Bassein signed between Bahadur Shah and the Portuguese?
masteryZone.sol: The Treaty of Bassein was signed on December 23, 1534.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following territories was ceded to the Portuguese Crown under the Treaty of Bassein?
opts: Bassein, Salsette, and the islands of Bombay
masteryZone.sol: The treaty ceded the province of Bassein, Salsette island, and the islands of Bombay.

masteryZone.q: Under the Treaty of Bassein, what restriction was placed on Gujarat's military ship building?
opts: No warships could be built without Portuguese consent
All warships must be painted blue
Only merchant vessels of over 500 tons could be built
Warships could only be constructed in Goa
masteryZone.sol: Sultan Bahadur Shah was prohibited from building warships without Portuguese consent.

masteryZone.q: Where were the ships of Gujarat required to pay duties under the Treaty of Bassein?
opts: At Portuguese customs houses in Bassein
masteryZone.sol: Gujarat's merchant vessels had to pay duties at Portuguese customs houses in Bassein.

masteryZone.q: What was the name of the Portuguese navigation license required for Gujarati merchant vessels after 1534?
masteryZone.sol: All Gujarati vessels had to obtain a Cartaz (licensing pass).

masteryZone.q: Why was Bassein highly valued by the Portuguese for their navy?
opts: It possessed vast forests of high-quality teak for shipbuilding
It was rich in silver mines
It had a direct canal connection to Goa
It was free from monsoon rains
masteryZone.sol: Bassein's dense teak forests provided excellent timber for repairing and building Portuguese ships.

masteryZone.q: Which cities did Humayun capture from Bahadur Shah, forcing the Sultan to seek Portuguese help?
masteryZone.sol: Humayun captured Mandu and Ahmedabad, which threatened Bahadur Shah's entire kingdom.

masteryZone.q: What military assistance did Nino da Cunha promise to Bahadur Shah in the 1534 treaty?
opts: A contingent of Portuguese soldiers and naval gunners
Control of the city of Delhi
masteryZone.sol: The Portuguese promised military aid, including soldiers and skilled gunners, to fight the Mughals.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following territories were acquired by Portugal via the Treaty of Bassein? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Bassein, Salsette, and Bombay were acquired in 1534. Diu was fortified later in 1535.

masteryZone.q: What restrictions were imposed on the Sultan of Gujarat by the 1534 treaty? (Select all that apply)
opts: Prohibition of building warships without Portuguese consent
Requirement to route merchant ships through Portuguese customs houses
Forced conversion of the Sultan's court to Christianity
Prohibition of forming alliances with the Ottoman Empire
masteryZone.sol: The treaty restricted warship construction and mandated customs routing. Conversion and Ottoman bans were not in the 1534 treaty.

masteryZone.q: Identify the strategic factors that made Bassein attractive to Nino da Cunha. (Select all that apply)
opts: Vast forests of teak wood for shipbuilding
Control over the northern shipping lanes of the Konkan
Access to agricultural revenue of the Bassein province
Rich gold mines on Salsette island
masteryZone.sol: Teak wood, shipping control, and land revenues made Bassein vital. There were no gold mines there.

masteryZone.q: Which major military conflicts were happening in northern India in 1534? (Select all that apply)
opts: Sher Shah Suri's rising rebellion in Bihar and Bengal
masteryZone.sol: Humayun's Gujarat campaign and Sher Shah Suri's rebellion were contemporary. British and Maratha conflicts occurred much later.

masteryZone.q: What terms did Bahadur Shah accept in exchange for Portuguese support? (Select all that apply)
opts: Cession of Bassein province and Bombay islands
Compulsory purchase of Cartazes for all merchant ships
Payment of customs duties at Portuguese stations
Surrender of the city of Ahmedabad to the Portuguese
masteryZone.sol: He ceded Bassein/Bombay, accepted Cartazes and customs duties. Ahmedabad was not surrendered to the Portuguese.

masteryZone.q: Select the regions that were part of the Bassein province ceded in 1534. (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Salsette, Thana coastal ports, and Bombay were part of the Bassein cession. Daman was not acquired in 1534.

masteryZone.q: Which individuals negotiated or signed the Treaty of Bassein? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Bahadur Shah and Nino da Cunha negotiated the treaty. Humayun was the enemy, and Vasco da Gama had died in 1524.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following best describe the Cartaz system under the Bassein treaty? (Select all that apply)
opts: It was a mandatory navigation pass for all Gujarati ships
It excluded ships from trading in contraband items like pepper and ginger
It was completely free of cost for the Sultan's personal fleet
It allowed Portuguese patrols to seize non-compliant vessels
masteryZone.sol: Cartazes were mandatory, prohibited specific contraband (spices/weapons), and allowed seizure. Even the Sultan's personal ships faced restrictions, though some personal exemptions were granted for small vessels, they still needed Cartazes.

masteryZone.q: What was the geopolitical impact of the 1534 treaty? (Select all that apply)
opts: It permanently secured a northern base for Portuguese shipbuilding
It weakened the naval sovereignty of the Gujarat Sultanate
It immediately led to the fall of the Mughal Empire
It brought the islands of Bombay under Portuguese control
masteryZone.sol: It secured shipbuilding assets, weakened Gujarat's naval power, and brought Bombay under Portugal. Humayun's empire did not fall.

masteryZone.q: Which trade goods from Bassein were highly prized by the Portuguese? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Bassein supplied teak wood, food grains, and salt. It had no gold mines.

masteryZone.q: The Treaty of Bassein was signed in the year 1534.
masteryZone.sol: The treaty was signed on December 23, 1534.

masteryZone.q: Bahadur Shah was forced to sign the treaty due to military pressure from the Mughal Emperor Akbar.
masteryZone.sol: It was Akbar's father, Humayun, who was invading Gujarat at that time.

masteryZone.q: Under the Treaty of Bassein, Bahadur Shah gave up his claim to the province of Bassein permanently.
masteryZone.sol: The province was ceded in perpetuity to the Portuguese Crown.

masteryZone.q: The Treaty of Bassein allowed Bahadur Shah to construct as many warships as he wanted.
masteryZone.sol: He was strictly prohibited from building warships without Portuguese authorization.

masteryZone.q: The seven islands of Bombay were part of the territory ceded in the 1534 treaty.
masteryZone.sol: The islands of Bombay were ceded as part of the Bassein territory.

masteryZone.q: Bahadur Shah signed the treaty aboard a Portuguese ship near the coast of Cochin.
masteryZone.sol: It was signed at Bassein on the Gujarat/Konkan border.

masteryZone.q: The Cartaz system allowed Gujarati ships to carry spices like pepper to any port in the world.
masteryZone.sol: Spices were declared Portuguese monopoly items (contraband) and could not be traded by private Indian ships.

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha led a joint military force to capture Ahmedabad alongside Bahadur Shah in 1534.
masteryZone.sol: The Portuguese provided defensive support and gunners, but did not join a march to recapture Ahmedabad immediately.

masteryZone.q: Bassein became the new capital of Portuguese India immediately after the 1534 treaty.
masteryZone.sol: Goa remained the official capital; Bassein was established as a northern fortress and province.

masteryZone.q: Salsette island was acquired by the Portuguese under the Treaty of Bassein.
masteryZone.sol: Salsette was ceded along with Bassein in 1534.

masteryZone.q: Mughal Emperor Humayun approved the Treaty of Bassein because he wanted to split Gujarat with the Portuguese.
masteryZone.sol: Humayun was entirely unaware/unsupportive of the treaty, as it was aimed directly against his expansion.

masteryZone.q: The Treaty of Bassein required all Gujarati merchant ships to pay duties at Portuguese customs stations.
masteryZone.sol: This term brought significant custom revenue to the Portuguese treasury.

masteryZone.q: The Treaty of Bassein was signed in the month of __________ in 1534.
masteryZone.sol: It was signed on December 23, 1534.

masteryZone.sol: Sultan Bahadur Shah signed the treaty.

masteryZone.sol: Humayun's invasion forced Bahadur Shah to seek help.

masteryZone.sol: He was restricted from building military warships.

masteryZone.sol: The navigation pass was the Cartaz.

masteryZone.sol: Customs duties had to be paid at Bassein customs houses.

masteryZone.sol: Governor Nino da Cunha negotiated the treaty.

masteryZone.sol: Salsette island was ceded alongside Bassein.

masteryZone.sol: Portuguese military gunners and soldiers were promised.

masteryZone.q: The Treaty of Bassein was signed in the year __________ CE.
masteryZone.sol: It was signed in 1534 CE.

masteryZone.q: Match the historical figures with their respective roles in the 1534 treaty crisis:
masteryZone.sol: Bahadur Shah was Sultan, da Cunha was Governor, and Humayun was Mughal Emperor.

masteryZone.q: Match the territories ceded in 1534 with their geographical descriptions:

options.text: Strategic island north of Bombay harbor
Seven small islands in the southern harbor

masteryZone.sol: Bassein is mainland, Salsette is northern island, Bombay is southern islands.

masteryZone.q: Match the terms of the Treaty of Bassein with their impacts:

options.text: Gave Portugal control of teakwood shipyards
Forced Gujarati merchants to pay duties

masteryZone.sol: Bassein cession gave teak control, Cartaz forced duties, and warship restriction demilitarized Gujarat's navy.

sections.title: 3. The Diu Fortification & Strategic Conflict with Bahadur Shah
sections.content:
Construction of the Diu Fort (1535): As Humayun's campaign in Gujarat intensified, Bahadur Shah granted the Portuguese permission to construct a stone fortress on the strategic island of Diu in 1535, in exchange for an immediate military alliance. The Portuguese built the Fort of Diu in record speed. However, by late 1536, the Mughal threat subsided as Humayun withdrew to Bengal to suppress the rebellion of Sher Shah Suri. Having secured his mainland territories, Bahadur Shah regretted ceding Diu and sought to reclaim the island.

Diplomatic Friction and Tensions: The relations between the Sultan and Governor Nino da Cunha deteriorated rapidly. The friction escalated over the division of Diu's customs revenues and the Portuguese construction of a partition wall, which separated their military sector from the Sultan's city. Fearing Portuguese encirclement, Bahadur Shah built counter-defenses and sent secret diplomatic missions to the Ottoman Sultan (Suleiman the Magnificent) and the Zamorin of Calicut, requesting naval fleets to expel the Portuguese from Diu.

masteryZone.q: In which year did Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat permit the Portuguese to build a fortress at Diu?
masteryZone.sol: Bahadur Shah granted permission to build the Diu Fort in 1535 CE.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Mughal threat to Gujarat suddenly decrease in late 1536?
opts: Humayun withdrew to Bengal to suppress Sher Shah Suri's rebellion
Humayun was defeated by the Portuguese fleet
masteryZone.sol: Humayun had to withdraw to Bengal to handle the rebellion of Sher Shah Suri.

masteryZone.q: What was the main source of financial conflict between Bahadur Shah and the Portuguese in Diu?
opts: The division of customs revenues collected at Diu port
masteryZone.sol: The dispute was over the division of lucrative customs revenues of Diu port.

masteryZone.q: What physical structure built by the Portuguese in Diu deeply offended Bahadur Shah?
opts: A partition wall separating the Portuguese fortress from the city
A new shipyard in the Sultan's personal harbor
A residential colony for Jesuit priests
masteryZone.sol: The Portuguese constructed a partition wall, dividing their fort area from the Sultan's city, which irritated Bahadur Shah.

masteryZone.q: To which Ottoman Sultan did Bahadur Shah send secret emissaries asking for naval help?
masteryZone.sol: Bahadur Shah sent letters requesting help from Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent.

masteryZone.q: Which local Indian ruler did Bahadur Shah attempt to ally with in order to expel the Portuguese from Diu?
masteryZone.sol: Bahadur Shah contacted the Zamorin of Calicut, a traditional Portuguese enemy.

masteryZone.q: Where is the strategic island of Diu located geographically?
opts: Off the southern coast of the Kathiawar peninsula of Gujarat
Near the mouth of the Zuari river
masteryZone.sol: Diu is situated just off the southern coast of Gujarat's Kathiawar peninsula.

masteryZone.q: What was Bahadur Shah's primary motive for allowing the Diu fort construction in 1535?
opts: To secure Portuguese military alliance against the invading Mughals
To build a joint merchant fleet for Europe
To convert his population to Christianity
To escape a rebellion in Surat
masteryZone.sol: He needed immediate military cooperation to halt Humayun's devastating invasion of Gujarat.

masteryZone.q: How did the Portuguese build the Fort of Diu in 1535?
opts: In record speed with materials and labor authorized by Bahadur Shah
Using imported Italian bricks and engineers
Over a period of twenty years
With the help of Mughal engineers sent by Humayun
masteryZone.sol: The fortress was constructed in record speed with the Sultan's cooperation.

masteryZone.q: Which Afghan leader's rebellion in the east forced Humayun to abandon his Gujarat campaign in 1536?
masteryZone.sol: Sher Shah Suri's rebellion in Bengal and Bihar forced Humayun to withdraw.

masteryZone.q: Which factors contributed to the deterioration of relations between Bahadur Shah and the Portuguese? (Select all that apply)
opts: The withdrawal of the Mughal threat in late 1536
Disagreements over the division of Diu customs revenues
The construction of a partition wall by the Portuguese in Diu
The conversion of Bahadur Shah's family to Catholicism
masteryZone.sol: Mughal withdrawal, customs disputes, and the partition wall caused the rift. No conversion of his family occurred.

masteryZone.q: Which regional powers did Bahadur Shah contact to build an anti-Portuguese alliance in 1536? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: He sent secret missions to the Ottomans and the Zamorin. The British and Dutch companies did not exist in India then.

masteryZone.q: What were the key characteristics of the Diu Fort built in 1535? (Select all that apply)
opts: Constructed of stone in record speed
Located on the eastern tip of Diu island
Fully financed and built by the Mughal army
Designed to control the entrance of the Gulf of Khambhat
masteryZone.sol: Diu Fort was stone-built, on the eastern tip, and controlled Khambhat's entrance. Mughals had no part in building it.

masteryZone.q: Why did Bahadur Shah regret ceding the fortification rights of Diu? (Select all that apply)
opts: He realized the Portuguese were fortifying the area beyond their agreed limits
The Mughal threat had disappeared by late 1536
The Portuguese refused to support him in recapturing Ahmedabad
The Ottoman fleet advised him that the Portuguese presence was dangerous
masteryZone.sol: Regret arose because the Mughal threat receded and the Portuguese fortified excessively. Ottoman fleets arrived only after his death.

masteryZone.q: Identify the geographical advantages of Diu for maritime control. (Select all that apply)
opts: Commanding position over the Gulf of Khambhat
Anchorage protected from the southwest monsoons
Proximity to the major trading ports of Surat and Cambay
Direct land borders connecting to Persia
masteryZone.sol: Diu commanded the Gulf, had protected monsoon anchorage, and was close to Surat/Cambay. It was an island, not bordered with Persia.

masteryZone.q: What defensive structures did Bahadur Shah build in Diu in response to the Portuguese partition wall? (Select all that apply)
opts: A counter-defense wall facing the Portuguese fortress
Fortified towers in the city sector
A new military harbor to block Portuguese shipping
A deep trench surrounding the entire island
masteryZone.sol: He built counter-walls and fortified city towers. He could not build a new harbor or dig an island trench.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following describes the partition wall in Diu? (Select all that apply)
opts: It separated the Portuguese fort sector from the Sultan's city
It caused massive friction and arguments between the two sides
It was requested by the local Hindu population for protection
It was built by the Portuguese under Governor Nino da Cunha's orders
masteryZone.sol: The wall separated the fort from the city, caused friction, and was ordered by da Cunha. Locals did not request it.

masteryZone.q: Which statements are correct about Humayun's campaign in Gujarat? (Select all that apply)
opts: He captured the key cities of Mandu and Ahmedabad
His campaign collapsed due to rebellions in the Bengal region
He was allied with the Zamorin of Calicut to expel the Portuguese
He withdrew completely from Gujarat by late 1536
masteryZone.sol: Humayun captured Mandu/Ahmedabad, withdrew due to Bengal rebellions, and left by late 1536. He had no alliance with the Zamorin.

masteryZone.q: What diplomatic strategies did Nino da Cunha use in Diu in 1536? (Select all that apply)

Refused to dismantle the controversial partition wall
Demanded a larger share of the customs revenues
Offered to surrender Bassein in exchange for peace in Diu

sections.title: 4. Expansion to Bengal (Hooghly) and San Thome (Madras)
sections.content:
Bengal Settlements (1536): Recognizing the immense wealth of the eastern delta, Nino da Cunha sent diplomatic missions to Bengal. In 1536, taking advantage of the conflict between Sultan Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah and the Afghan leader Sher Shah Suri, the Portuguese secured permission to establish factories. They established two major settlements: Porto Pequeno (Little Port) at Hooghly on the Bhagirathi river, and Porto Grande (Great Port) at Chittagong. These ports handled exports of saltpetre, raw silk, sugar, and fine muslin. The Bengal operations were unique because they were dominated by private Portuguese merchants (casados) operating outside the official Crown monopoly.

Establishment of San Thome (Mylapore): On the Coromandel Coast, Portuguese private traders and missionaries established the settlement of San Thome near Mylapore. The settlement was centered around the tomb of St. Thomas the Apostle, making it both a religious pilgrimage site and a major commercial port. San Thome exported textiles to Malacca and the Far East, linking the Coromandel trade directly into the Portuguese Asian maritime network without requiring heavy royal military investments.

masteryZone.q: In which year did the Portuguese establish factories in Bengal under Nino da Cunha's administration?
masteryZone.sol: The factories in Bengal were established in 1536 CE.

masteryZone.q: Which Bengal Sultan permitted the Portuguese to establish factories at Hooghly and Chittagong?
masteryZone.sol: Sultan Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah granted the permissions to secure Portuguese military help.

masteryZone.q: What was the Portuguese name for the settlement established at Hooghly?
masteryZone.sol: The settlement at Hooghly was named Porto Pequeno (Little Port).

masteryZone.q: What was the Portuguese name for the settlement established at Chittagong?
masteryZone.sol: Chittagong was named Porto Grande (Great Port) by the Portuguese.

masteryZone.q: On which river is the settlement of Hooghly (Porto Pequeno) located?
masteryZone.sol: Hooghly is located on the Bhagirathi river branch of the Ganges delta.

masteryZone.q: Which group of Portuguese nationals dominated the trade and settlement in Bengal outside official Crown control?
masteryZone.sol: Private Portuguese merchants known as casados dominated the Bengal trade.

masteryZone.q: Which Portuguese settlement was established on the Coromandel Coast near Madras?
masteryZone.sol: The settlement of San Thome was established near Mylapore, Madras.

masteryZone.q: Which Christian Apostle's shrine was the focal point of the San Thome settlement?
masteryZone.sol: San Thome was built around the shrine and tomb of St. Thomas the Apostle.

masteryZone.q: What was the main export item shipped from San Thome to Malacca?
masteryZone.sol: Coromandel textiles (cotton goods) were the primary export from San Thome.

masteryZone.q: Which conflict in Bengal did the Portuguese exploit to gain their trading rights in 1536?
opts: The conflict between Sultan Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah and Sher Shah Suri
The Mughal invasion of Chittagong by Humayun
A rebellion by the local zamindars
A naval war with the Arakan kingdom
masteryZone.sol: The Portuguese exploited the conflict between Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah and Sher Shah Suri to offer military assistance in exchange for trade rights.

masteryZone.q: Which settlements in Bengal were authorized by the Sultan of Bengal in 1536? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Porto Pequeno and Porto Grande were established in Bengal. San Thome was in Madras (Coromandel), and Fort Manuel was in Cochin.

masteryZone.q: Which trade goods were exported from the Portuguese Bengal settlements? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Bengal exported saltpetre, textiles/muslin, silk, and sugar. Horses were imported in Goa, not exported from Bengal.

masteryZone.q: What was unique about the Portuguese presence in Bengal compared to Goa? (Select all that apply)
opts: It was dominated by private merchants (casados) rather than the Crown
It operated outside the strict royal monopoly system
No Catholic missionaries were allowed in Bengal
The settlements lacked formal stone fortresses owned by the Crown
masteryZone.sol: Bengal was casados-dominated, lacked Crown fortress control, and operated loosely. Missionaries were allowed and active.

masteryZone.q: Identify the features of the San Thome settlement near Madras. (Select all that apply)
opts: Established near the shrine of St. Thomas the Apostle
Centered on the Coromandel textile export trade
Directly governed by a royal Viceroy appointed from Lisbon
Formed by private Portuguese merchants and missionaries
masteryZone.sol: San Thome was centered on the shrine, Coromandel textiles, and casados. It had no resident Viceroy.

masteryZone.q: Which rivers or delta branches were associated with Portuguese eastern expansion? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The Bhagirathi (Hooghly) and Karnafuli (Chittagong) rivers were centers of Bengal expansion.

masteryZone.q: What benefits did Sultan Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah hope to gain from the Portuguese? (Select all that apply)
opts: Portuguese naval defense and gunners against Sher Shah Suri
Access to Portuguese horse imports in Bengal
Help in conquering the Delhi Sultanate
Guns and ammunition for his troops
masteryZone.sol: He wanted military gunners, naval help, and arms against Sher Shah. Delhi conquests and horse imports were not part of this.

masteryZone.q: Identify the export destinations linked directly to the San Thome textile trade. (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: San Thome textiles were shipped to Malacca and China (Macau). London and Amsterdam were not Portuguese hubs.

masteryZone.q: Which statements are correct regarding the distinction between Porto Grande and Porto Pequeno? (Select all that apply)
opts: Porto Grande was located on the Bhagirathi River
Both were established under Governor Nino da Cunha in 1536
masteryZone.sol: Grande is Chittagong, Pequeno is Hooghly, and both were founded in 1536. Grande was on the Karnafuli, not the Bhagirathi.

masteryZone.q: Select the roles played by Catholic missionaries in San Thome. (Select all that apply)
opts: Established churches and parishes around the St. Thomas shrine
Served as official naval commanders of Portuguese fleets
Provided religious oversight to the private traders (casados)
masteryZone.sol: Missionaries built churches, conducted conversions, and oversaw the casados. They were not naval commanders.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following factors favored Portuguese trade in the Bengal Delta? (Select all that apply)
opts: Rich agricultural productivity of the Bengal hinterland
Excellent network of river channels for boat transport
Absence of any local taxation by Bengal Sultans
High demand for Bengal textiles in Southeast Asia
masteryZone.sol: Bengal's agriculture, river channels, and textile demand favored trade. Local taxes were imposed by the Sultan.

masteryZone.q: Porto Grande was the Portuguese name for Hooghly.
masteryZone.sol: Porto Grande was Chittagong, while Porto Pequeno was Hooghly.

masteryZone.q: The settlements in Bengal were established in the year 1536.
masteryZone.sol: They were established under Governor Nino da Cunha in 1536.

masteryZone.q: San Thome was founded on the Malabar coast of western India.
masteryZone.sol: San Thome was established on the Coromandel coast of eastern India near Madras.

masteryZone.q: The settlement of San Thome was built around the tomb of St. Thomas the Apostle.
masteryZone.sol: It was a major religious shrine and pilgrimage site for Portuguese Christians.

masteryZone.q: The Bengal trade was managed under a strict royal monopoly with a large Crown fleet stationed at Hooghly.
masteryZone.sol: It was run mostly by private merchants (casados) with very limited direct Crown military involvement.

masteryZone.q: Sultan Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah of Bengal was an ally of Sher Shah Suri in 1536.
masteryZone.sol: They were bitter enemies fighting for control of Bengal.

sections.title: 5. Decline of Gujarat Alliance & Historical Legacy of Nino da Cunha
sections.content:
The Death of Bahadur Shah (1537): In February 1537, Governor Nino da Cunha arrived at Diu to negotiate with the Sultan. During a meeting held aboard the Governor's vessel in Diu harbor, mutual suspicions and high tensions led to a spontaneous physical scuffle between the Sultan's retinue and Portuguese guards. In the chaos, Bahadur Shah fell into the harbor and drowned. His sudden death without a designated direct male heir triggered a succession crisis in Gujarat and allowed the Portuguese to seize absolute military control of Diu's fortifications.

The Siege of Diu (1538) and Recall: The Ottoman Empire responded to the late Sultan's pleas by sending a massive naval fleet commanded by Suleiman Pasha, governor of Egypt. In 1538, the joint Ottoman and Gujarat forces besieged the Diu Fort. The Portuguese garrison, commanded by Antonio da Silveira, successfully defended the fort against overwhelming odds until the Ottomans withdrew. Despite this success, da Cunha's controversial actions, court intrigues, and administrative complaints led to his recall in 1538. He was succeeded by Garcia de Noronha. Nino da Cunha died at sea in 1539 during his return voyage to Lisbon, leaving behind a consolidated northern maritime empire.

masteryZone.q: On what date did Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat drown during a visit to Governor Nino da Cunha's ship?
masteryZone.sol: Bahadur Shah drowned on February 13, 1537, following a violent clash aboard the Portuguese vessel off Diu.

masteryZone.q: Who succeeded Nino da Cunha as the Governor of Portuguese India in 1538?
masteryZone.sol: Garcia de Noronha succeeded Nino da Cunha as Governor in 1538.

masteryZone.q: Where did Nino da Cunha die in 1539 on his return journey to Portugal?
opts: At sea near the Cape of Good Hope
masteryZone.sol: Nino da Cunha died at sea near the Cape of Good Hope during his voyage back to Lisbon.

masteryZone.q: Which Ottoman commander led the powerful naval fleet that besieged Diu in 1538?
masteryZone.sol: Suleiman Pasha, Governor of Ottoman Egypt, commanded the fleet that besieged Diu in 1538.

masteryZone.q: Who was the captain of the Diu fortress who successfully defended it during the Ottoman siege of 1538?
masteryZone.sol: António da Silveira was the captain who led the heroic defense of the Diu fortress.

masteryZone.q: What was the main outcome of the Siege of Diu in 1538 for Portuguese power in India?
opts: The Portuguese successfully repulsed the joint Ottoman-Gujarat siege
The fortress of Diu was completely destroyed and abandoned
Goa was captured by the Ottomans
The Portuguese were forced to pay tribute to the Ottoman Sultan
masteryZone.sol: The Portuguese successfully held Diu, proving their maritime and defensive fortress superiority.

masteryZone.q: What was the tragic fate of Bahadur Shah's body after his death in 1537?
opts: It was never recovered from the sea
It was buried in the grand mosque of Diu
It was taken to Ahmedabad for a royal funeral
It was returned to the Mughal Emperor Humayun
masteryZone.sol: His body drowned in the ocean waters and was never recovered.

masteryZone.q: Why was Governor Nino da Cunha recalled to Portugal in disgrace in 1538?
opts: Due to charges of financial corruption and the controversial death of Bahadur Shah
Because he lost Goa to the Sultan of Bijapur
Because he refused to convert to Christianity
For failing to establish trade in Bengal
masteryZone.sol: Charges of administrative abuses, financial corruption, and the political scandal of Bahadur Shah's death led to his recall.

masteryZone.q: How did the King of Portugal honor the late Nino da Cunha despite his recall in disgrace?
opts: His debts were cleared and his memory was cleared of all charges posthumously
A statue was built in Lisbon immediately
His family was exiled to India permanently
He was declared a Saint by the Church
masteryZone.sol: His father, Nuno da Cunha, cleared his debts, and the Crown later recognized his immense contributions by clearing his name.

masteryZone.q: What administrative region consolidated by Nino da Cunha became known as the 'Província do Norte'?
opts: The coastal territory from Chaul to Diu including Bassein
masteryZone.sol: The 'Província do Norte' comprised Bassein, Salsette, Bombay, Daman, and Diu.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following factors led to the death of Bahadur Shah of Gujarat? (Select all that apply)
opts: Distrust during his visit to Nino da Cunha's ship
A sudden physical scuffle and brawl on board
His inability to swim when he fell or jumped into the sea
An Ottoman cannon strike on his boat
masteryZone.sol: Distrust, a physical scuffle, and drowning caused his death. No Ottoman attack occurred at that moment.

masteryZone.q: Identify the participants in the Siege of Diu in 1538. (Select all that apply)
opts: The Ottoman fleet under Suleiman Pasha
The land forces of the Gujarat Sultanate
The Portuguese garrison defending the fort
The Mughal army led by Emperor Humayun
masteryZone.sol: The siege was a joint Ottoman-Gujarat action against the defending Portuguese. Mughals were not involved.

masteryZone.q: What reforms did Nino da Cunha introduce to stabilize the newly acquired Northern Province? (Select all that apply)
opts: Regulation of customs houses in Bassein and Diu
Distribution of land grants (aforamentos) to Portuguese settlers
Minting of Portuguese coinage in Diu
Expulsion of all Muslim merchants from Gujarat
masteryZone.sol: Da Cunha regulated customs, issued land grants, and minted coins. He did not expel Muslim merchants.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following territories were part of the Portuguese 'Província do Norte'? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The Northern Province included Bassein, Salsette, Diu, Daman, and Bombay. Calicut/Cochin were in the South.

masteryZone.q: Select the reasons why the Ottoman forces abandoned the Siege of Diu in 1538. (Select all that apply)
opts: Severe internal division and mutual suspicion between the Ottomans and the Gujarat Sultanate
The heroic defense and heavy casualties inflicted by the Portuguese garrison
Rumors of the arrival of a massive Portuguese relief fleet from Goa
The capture of Cairo by the Portuguese Navy
masteryZone.sol: Internal divisions, Portuguese resistance, and rumors of a relief fleet led to the Ottoman withdrawal. Cairo was not captured.

masteryZone.q: What charges were levied against Nino da Cunha that led to his replacement? (Select all that apply)
opts: Financial corruption and misappropriation of revenues
The diplomatic embarrassment of Bahadur Shah's death
Failure to defend Diu from the Ottomans
masteryZone.sol: Charges of corruption and the scandal surrounding the Sultan's death caused his recall. He did not fail in Diu or Bengal.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following statements are true about the death and burial of Nino da Cunha? (Select all that apply)
opts: He died aboard his flagship near the Cape of Good Hope
His body was committed to the sea in a simple coffin
He was buried with full royal honors in the Lisbon Cathedral
He died in absolute poverty before reaching Portugal
masteryZone.sol: He died at sea, was buried at sea in a simple coffin, and died with heavy debts. He was not buried in Lisbon Cathedral.

masteryZone.q: Identify the accomplishments of Nino da Cunha's decade-long rule. (Select all that apply)
opts: Transfer of the Portuguese capital from Cochin to Goa in 1530
Acquisition of Bassein and the islands of Bombay in 1534
Securing and fortifying the strategic island of Diu in 1535
Conquest of the entire Maldives archipelago
masteryZone.sol: Capital transfer, Bassein acquisition, and Diu fortifying were his key legacy achievements. Maldives was not conquered.

masteryZone.q: Who were the key Portuguese commanders involved in the Diu conflict between 1535 and 1538? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: De Sousa, Silveira, and da Cunha were actively involved. Albuquerque died in 1515.

masteryZone.q: What was the long-term significance of the 'Província do Norte' for the Estado da Índia? (Select all that apply)
opts: It became the second most important revenue-producing region after Goa
It provided critical raw materials like timber and salt for Portuguese fleets
It secured the northern flank of Portuguese maritime control in the Arabian Sea
It served as a land route to export goods to China
masteryZone.sol: It was a major revenue generator, supplied ship timber, and secured the northern trade. It was not a land route to China.

masteryZone.q: Bahadur Shah died by falling from a horse during a polo match in Diu.
masteryZone.sol: He drowned in the sea following a physical conflict aboard a Portuguese ship in February 1537.

masteryZone.q: Suleiman Pasha led the Ottoman fleet in the Siege of Diu in 1538.
masteryZone.sol: He was the Ottoman commander sent by the Sultan of Egypt/Ottoman Sultan to attack Diu.

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha was buried with full royal state honors in Lisbon Cathedral.
masteryZone.sol: He died at sea and his body was buried in the ocean off the Cape of Good Hope.

masteryZone.q: The Portuguese successfully defended Diu in the siege of 1538.
masteryZone.sol: The garrison held out heroically, causing the Ottomans to abandon the siege.

masteryZone.q: Garcia de Noronha succeeded Nino da Cunha as Governor of Portuguese India.
masteryZone.sol: Noronha arrived in 1538 to assume the office of Governor.

masteryZone.q: Bahadur Shah's body was recovered and placed in a marble tomb in Ahmedabad.
masteryZone.sol: His body was lost in the sea and never recovered.

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha served as Governor of Portuguese India for approximately ten years.
masteryZone.sol: His tenure lasted from late 1529 until late 1538.

masteryZone.q: The Província do Norte included territories on both the eastern and western coasts of India.
masteryZone.sol: It was strictly comprised of western coastal territories north of Goa (Bassein, Diu, Daman, Bombay).

masteryZone.q: The Ottoman fleet failed to capture Diu partly due to coordination failures with the local Gujarati forces.
masteryZone.sol: Deep distrust between Suleiman Pasha and the Gujarat Sultanate army led to coordination breakdown.

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha died in deep financial debt.
masteryZone.sol: He was in debt at the time of his death, which his father later resolved with the Crown.

masteryZone.q: Manuel de Sousa was the Viceroy who succeeded Garcia de Noronha.
masteryZone.sol: Noronha was succeeded by Estevão da Gama, not Manuel de Sousa.

masteryZone.q: The defense of Diu in 1538 was led by Captain António da Silveira.
masteryZone.sol: Silveira commanded the small Portuguese force that successfully resisted the massive siege.

masteryZone.q: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat died by __________ in 1537.
masteryZone.sol: He drowned in the sea after a violent scuffle.

masteryZone.q: The Ottoman fleet that attacked Diu in 1538 was commanded by __________ Pasha.
masteryZone.sol: Suleiman Pasha commanded the Ottoman naval forces.

masteryZone.q: Governor Nino da Cunha was replaced in 1538 by Garcia de __________.
masteryZone.sol: Garcia de Noronha assumed the office of Governor in 1538.

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha died at sea near the Cape of Good __________.
masteryZone.sol: He died near the Cape of Good Hope on his voyage back.

masteryZone.q: The heroic captain who defended Diu Fort during the 1538 siege was António da __________.
masteryZone.sol: António da Silveira led the defense.

masteryZone.q: The administrative division consolidated by da Cunha was known as the Province of the __________.
masteryZone.sol: It was called the Northern Province (Província do Norte).

masteryZone.q: Bahadur Shah visited the Portuguese flagship on February 13, __________ CE.
masteryZone.sol: He visited and died on February 13, 1537.

masteryZone.q: The body of Sultan Bahadur Shah was never __________ from the ocean.
masteryZone.sol: It was lost at sea and never recovered.

masteryZone.q: Nino da Cunha's father who cleared his debts was __________ da Cunha.
masteryZone.sol: Nuno da Cunha was his father.

masteryZone.q: The coin minted by the Portuguese in Diu was the silver __________.
masteryZone.sol: The bazaruco was a local currency minted by the Portuguese.

masteryZone.q: The Siege of Diu in 1538 was abandoned by the Ottomans in the month of __________.
masteryZone.sol: The siege was abandoned in November 1538.

masteryZone.q: The fortress of Diu was built at the eastern __________ of Diu island.
masteryZone.sol: It was built at the eastern tip of Diu.

masteryZone.q: Match the historical figures with their places of death:

options.text: At sea near Cape of Good Hope
At sea near Goa harbor entrance

masteryZone.sol: Bahadur Shah drowned off Diu, da Cunha died near Cape of Good Hope, Albuquerque died near Goa harbor.

masteryZone.q: Match the offices and roles held during the Diu Siege of 1538:
masteryZone.sol: Silveira was Fortress Captain, Suleiman Pasha was Ottoman Commander, Noronha was Governor.

masteryZone.q: Match the events with their chronological order in Nino da Cunha's life:
masteryZone.sol: Capital transfer was 1530, Bassein was 1534, and Bahadur Shah's death was 1537.

masteryZone.q: Match the coins and fiscal terms with their descriptions:

options.text: Portuguese silver coin minted in Diu
Land grant issued to Portuguese settlers
Primary source of fiscal dispute in Diu

masteryZone.sol: Bazaruco was coin, aforamento was land grant, customs split was primary dispute.

masteryZone.q: Match the geographic sectors of the Província do Norte with their values:

options.text: Commanded the trade of Kathiawar coast

masteryZone.sol: Bassein provided teak, Diu commanded Kathiawar, Salsette was agricultural hinterland.

masteryZone.q: Match the military failures of the 1538 siege with their reasons:

options.text: Internal suspicion and threat of Portuguese relief fleet
Loss of their Sultan and leadership divisions
Preoccupation with eastern rebellions of Sher Shah

masteryZone.sol: Ottoman retreat was due to suspicion/relief threat, Gujarat failure due to Sultan loss, Mughal inactivity due to Sher Shah.

masteryZone.q: On which ship did Bahadur Shah of Gujarat die in 1537?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: Governor Nino da Cunha's flagship. Explanation: He died off the coast of Diu during a meeting with the Governor.

masteryZone.q: Who succeeded Governor Garcia de Noronha?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: Estevão da Gama. Explanation: Estevão da Gama, son of Vasco da Gama, became governor in 1540.

masteryZone.q: In which year did the Ottoman fleet lift the Siege of Diu?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: 1538 CE. Explanation: The siege was abandoned in November 1538 after several months of failing to breach the fortress.

masteryZone.q: Where was Nino da Cunha buried after his death at sea?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: He was buried at sea near the Cape of Good Hope. Explanation: His body was committed to the ocean in a simple coffin.

masteryZone.q: What was the name of the Portuguese land grant system used in Bassein?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: Aforamento. Explanation: Aforamento allowed lands to be granted to Portuguese settlers in exchange for quit-rents.

masteryZone.q: Who was the ruler of the Gujarat Sultanate during the Siege of Diu in 1538?
masteryZone.sol: Answer: Mahmud Shah III. Explanation: Mahmud Shah III succeeded Bahadur Shah and participated in the joint siege.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Bahadur Shah's body was entombed in the grand cathedral of Goa.
Reason: The Portuguese wanted to show high respect to the deceased Sultan of Gujarat.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are false; Bahadur Shah's body drowned in the sea off Diu and was never recovered.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Nino da Cunha was recalled to Portugal in disgrace in 1538.
Reason: He was charged with administrative failures, corruption, and creating diplomatic scandal over the Sultan's death.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The corruption charges and the scandal of Bahadur Shah's death directly caused the Portuguese Crown to recall da Cunha.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: The Ottoman siege of Diu in 1538 was a complete success.
Reason: Suleiman Pasha managed to demolish the entire Diu fortress and capture the Portuguese garrison.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are false; the siege was a failure, and the Portuguese successfully defended the fortress under António da Silveira.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Garcia de Noronha succeeded Nino da Cunha as the Governor of Portuguese India in 1538.
Reason: The Portuguese Crown wanted to clean up the corruption associated with da Cunha's administration.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The Crown sent Noronha as Governor to replace da Cunha and restore order and integrity to the administration.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: The Província do Norte became a key source of revenue for the Portuguese empire.
Reason: It possessed valuable agricultural land, salt pans, and shipbuilding teak wood.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The resources and trade of the Northern Province made it highly profitable and second in importance only to Goa.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Nino da Cunha built a tomb for himself in Diu prior to his departure.
Reason: He knew he would die during his voyage back to Portugal.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are false; he did not build a tomb in Diu, and he did not anticipate his death at sea.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the capital shift in 1530:
1. It was ordered by Lopo Vaz de Sampaio before his arrest.
2. It officially designated Goa as the headquarters of the Estado da Índia.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is false because Nino da Cunha ordered the shift, not Sampaio. Statement 2 is true.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Treaty of Bassein (1534):
1. The treaty was signed between Governor Nino da Cunha and Sultan Bahadur Shah.
2. The Portuguese gained control over Bassein and the island of Salsette.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. The treaty ceded Bassein and Salsette to the Portuguese.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Portuguese expansion in Bengal, consider the following:
1. Hooghly was designated as Porto Pequeno by the Portuguese.
2. The Crown directly managed all Bengal factories through a royal captain.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false as the Bengal trade was dominated by private merchants (casados) without formal Crown fortress control.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the death of Bahadur Shah of Gujarat:
1. He drowned during a sudden violent dispute on board Nino da Cunha's ship.
2. His body was recovered and entombed in Diu's central cathedral.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false; his body was never recovered from the sea.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 1538 Siege of Diu:
1. The defending Portuguese forces were led by Governor Garcia de Noronha himself.
2. The attacking coalition included a powerful fleet sent by the Ottoman Empire.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is false because Captain António da Silveira led the defense. Statement 2 is true.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the administration of Nino da Cunha, consider the following:
1. The capital transfer from Cochin to Goa occurred in 1530.
2. The high court 'Relação' and the royal treasury were shifted to Goa to centralize authority.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. The capital shift involved moving the judicial and fiscal machinery to Goa.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Cartaz system under the Treaty of Bassein:
1. Gujarati merchant ships had to pay duties to the Portuguese at Bassein.
2. The Gujarat Sultan was allowed to build warships without any restrictions.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false because Bahadur Shah was prohibited from building warships.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about San Thome near Madras:
1. It was founded primarily by private traders and Franciscan/Jesuit missionaries.
2. It served as a vital link for the export of Coromandel textiles to Malacca.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. San Thome was a private trade hub linked with the tomb of St. Thomas.

practiceQuestions.q:
Regarding the predecessor and successor of Nino da Cunha, consider the following:
1. Lopo Vaz de Sampaio succeeded da Cunha in 1538.
2. Garcia de Noronha succeeded Lopo Vaz de Sampaio in 1529.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are false. Da Cunha succeeded Sampaio in 1529 and Noronha succeeded da Cunha in 1538.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the partition wall in Diu, consider the following statements:
1. It was built by Bahadur Shah to fortify the Gujarati sector against the Portuguese.
2. It divided the Portuguese military garrison from the local civilian Gujarati city.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is false; it was built by the Portuguese. Statement 2 is true.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the trade of Chittagong (Porto Grande) in Bengal:
1. It was the primary port for exporting fine muslin to Portuguese Malacca.
2. The Portuguese Crown maintained a large permanent navy there to enforce cartazes.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false as Bengal was managed by private traders with minimal official navy presence.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mughal Emperor Humayun's role in the Diu crisis:
1. His invasion of Gujarat forced Bahadur Shah to seek a Portuguese alliance in 1534.
2. His subsequent retreat to Bengal relieved pressure on Gujarat, causing Bahadur Shah to regret the treaty.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. Humayun's campaigns directly dictated Bahadur Shah's shifting policy toward the Portuguese.

practiceQuestions.q:
Regarding the economic assets of Bassein, consider the following:
1. Bassein was a major supplier of high-quality teak timber for building Portuguese ships.
2. It lacked agricultural productivity and relied entirely on grain imports from Goa.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false because Bassein was highly productive agriculturally and exported rice and vegetables to Goa.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Portuguese 'Província do Norte':
1. It included the territories of Chaul, Bassein, Daman, Diu, and Bombay.
2. It was governed by a separate Viceroy appointed directly from Lisbon.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false because it was subordinate to the Governor/Viceroy in Goa.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the death of Nino da Cunha:
1. He passed away peacefully in Lisbon after receiving a state pension.
2. He died during his voyage back to Portugal and was buried at sea near the Cape of Good Hope.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true. He died at sea in 1539 in deep debt.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the first Siege of Diu (1538), consider the following:
1. The siege was defended by the Portuguese captain António da Silveira.
2. Suleiman Pasha led the joint land and naval assault but abandoned the effort.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. Silveira's defense and Pasha's retreat saved Portuguese Diu.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Bengal Sultan Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah:
1. He granted the Portuguese rights to build factories in exchange for help against Sher Shah Suri.
2. He was successfully reinstated to his throne by the Portuguese army in 1538.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false because Sher Shah Suri defeated the Sultan and captured Bengal.

practiceQuestions.q:
Regarding the fiscal policies of Nino da Cunha, consider the following statements:
1. He established customs houses in newly acquired Bassein to collect trade duties.
2. He introduced the silver bazaruco coin to stabilize monetary exchange in Diu.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. These fiscal measures helped consolidate Portuguese administrative control.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Portuguese trade in the Indian Ocean:
1. The capital Goa served as the central node for Arabian horse imports.
2. Cochin ceased to have any commercial value after the capital shifted to Goa.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false because Cochin remained a major center for pepper collection and export.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the geographic division of Bengal trade ports:
1. Porto Pequeno was located at Hooghly on the Bhagirathi branch.
2. Porto Grande was located at Chittagong on the Karnafuli branch.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. These two branches defined the eastern and western ends of the Bengal delta trade.

practiceQuestions.q:
Regarding the defense of Portuguese India, consider the following:
1. Under Sampaio, the Portuguese built the massive fortress of Bassein.
2. Under da Cunha, the Diu fortress was secured and fortified in 1535.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is false because Bassein was acquired and fortified under Nino da Cunha. Statement 2 is true.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Portuguese actions in Diu after Bahadur Shah's death:
1. They immediately seized control of Diu's main customs house.
2. They appointed Manuel de Sousa as the permanent captain of the Diu fortress.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. The sudden demise of Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to assert complete fiscal and military control.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the land tenure system in Portuguese Bassein:
1. The land was divided into grants called aforamentos.
2. Settlers who received these grants were exempted from military service.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false because landholders were obligated to provide military service in times of war.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the trade between Madras (San Thome) and Southeast Asia, consider the following:
1. Coromandel cotton textiles were traded for spices and porcelain in Malacca.
2. The trade route was strictly monitored by royal Portuguese warships based in Mylapore.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false as the port of San Thome was unregulated by direct royal warships and run by private traders.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the recall of Governor Nino da Cunha:
1. He was accused of extreme corruption by factions inside the Goa administration.
2. The Portuguese King cleared his name posthumously after his father paid off his debts.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. His father Nuno da Cunha's actions and the political adjustments cleared his legacy.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the Portuguese settlements with their local Indian states:
practiceQuestions.sol: Goa was taken from Bijapur, Bassein from Gujarat, and Porto Pequeno was in Bengal.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the key treaty clauses of 1534 with their target sectors:
practiceQuestions.sol: Cession was territorial, Cartaz was mercantile monopoly, and warship ban was demilitarization.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the ports with their geographical river/marine bodies:
practiceQuestions.sol: Porto Pequeno was on Bhagirathi, Porto Grande on Karnafuli, San Thome on Coromandel.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the Portuguese administrators with their primary historical actions:

options.text: Predecessor arrested and sent in chains

practiceQuestions.sol: Da Cunha shifted capital, Sampaio was sent in chains, Noronha succeeded da Cunha.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the Diu siege figures of 1538 with their affiliations:
practiceQuestions.sol: Silveira was Portuguese captain, Pasha was Ottoman commander, Mahmud III was Gujarat Sultan.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the historical locations with their primary exports/assets:
practiceQuestions.sol: Bassein supplied teak, Hooghly supplied saltpetre/sugar, San Thome exported textiles.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the chronological dates with the key historical events:

options.text: Signing of the Treaty of Bassein
Death of Bahadur Shah in Diu

practiceQuestions.sol: Capital shift was 1530, Bassein Treaty was 1534, Bahadur Shah died in 1537.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the coin types with their respective descriptions:

options.text: Portuguese silver/copper coin minted in Diu
Portuguese gold coin used in global trade
Gold currency commonly traded in western India

practiceQuestions.sol: Bazaruco was local Diu coin, Cruzado was gold coin of Portugal, Pardao was local gold coin.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the historical causes with their political effects under Nino da Cunha:

options.text: Forced the Treaty of Bassein in 1534
Gave Portuguese complete control of Diu Fort
Led to the appointment of Garcia de Noronha

practiceQuestions.sol: Humayun's invasion caused the Bassein treaty, Bahadur's death secured Diu Fort, da Cunha's recall led to Noronha's arrival.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the Bengal delta administrative terms with their operational meanings:
practiceQuestions.sol: Porto Pequeno is Hooghly, Porto Grande is Chittagong, Casados are private married settlers.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the military fortresses with their construction years under Portuguese rule:

options.text: Built in 1535 during alliance with Bahadur Shah

practiceQuestions.sol: Goa was 1510, Bassein was built after 1534, Diu was built in 1535.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the saints and religious monuments with their locations on the Coromandel coast:

options.text: The sacred burial site of the Apostle
The commercial Portuguese colony near Madras
The historical Indian town hosting the shrine

practiceQuestions.sol: St. Thomas Tomb is the burial site, San Thome is the colony, Mylapore is the hosting town.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the European powers with their rivals in the Indian Ocean in 1538:

options.text: Sent fleet from Egypt to counter Portuguese
Allied with Ottomans to reclaim local ports

practiceQuestions.sol: Portuguese defended, Ottomans sent fleet from Egypt, Gujarat allied with Ottomans.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the administrative terms with their locations or actions:

options.text: High Court established in Goa capital
Land lease contract system for Bassein settlers

practiceQuestions.sol: Relação was High Court, Chancelaria was Royal Treasury, aforamento was land lease system.

practiceQuestions.q: Match the final outcomes of Portuguese governors with their post-tenure status:

options.text: Died at sea near Cape of Good Hope in 1539
Sent to Lisbon in chains in 1529
Killed by Khoikhoi in South Africa in 1510

practiceQuestions.sol: Da Cunha died at sea, Sampaio was sent in chains, Almeida was killed in South Africa.

practiceQuestions.q:

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Goa was selected for its defensibility and horse trade, not because it was closer to Malabar spice regions (Cochin is closer).

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion: The Treaty of Bassein ceding Salsette and Bombay was signed in 1534.
Reason: Sultan Bahadur Shah faced an existential threat from the Mughal Emperor Humayun.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mughal threat from Humayun forced the Sultan to sign the treaty to secure Portuguese military help.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion: The Portuguese Bengal trade did not rely on formal military fortresses.
Reason: The trade was conducted by private merchants (casados) outside the Crown's direct control.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: The absence of a Crown fortress was because Bengal trade was run by private casados acting independently.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat regretted ceding Diu to the Portuguese by late 1536.
Reason: Emperor Humayun had withdrawn his forces from Gujarat to address Sher Shah's rebellion in Bengal.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: The removal of the Mughal threat meant Bahadur Shah no longer needed the Portuguese alliance and wanted Diu back.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion: The partition wall in Diu was a source of severe conflict between Bahadur Shah and the Portuguese.
Reason: The wall physically cut off the Sultan's city from the strategic harbor and the fortress.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: The wall built by the Portuguese restricted the Sultan's access and sovereignty over his own city's defense, leading to conflict.

practiceQuestions.q:

Reason: The Ottoman naval fleet had superior artillery that destroyed the Portuguese outer walls.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

mockTestQuestions.q: Which of the following ports was known as 'Porto Pequeno' under Nino da Cunha's Bengal administration?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Porto Pequeno was Hooghly, whereas Porto Grande was Chittagong.

mockTestQuestions.q: In which year did the Portuguese officially shift the capital of the Estado da Índia from Cochin to Goa?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The capital shift was carried out by Nino da Cunha in 1530.

mockTestQuestions.q: What was the main reason Sultan Bahadur Shah signed the Treaty of Bassein in 1534?
opts: To secure Portuguese military assistance against the Mughal Emperor Humayun
To establish joint spice trade monopolies in Malacca
To surrender his entire kingdom and retire to Lisbon
To build a combined navy to attack the Ottoman Empire
mockTestQuestions.sol: The imminent Mughal invasion by Humayun forced the Sultan to seek Portuguese military backing.

mockTestQuestions.q: The military defense of the Diu fortress in 1538 against the Ottoman fleet was commanded by whom?
mockTestQuestions.sol: António da Silveira commanded the defense of the besieged Diu fortress.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which of the following territories was NOT ceded to the Portuguese under the 1534 Treaty of Bassein?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Diu was only fortified later in 1535. Bassein, Salsette, and Bombay were ceded under the 1534 treaty.

mockTestQuestions.q: What was the unique feature of the Portuguese settlements in Bengal during Nino da Cunha's tenure?
opts: They were run by private merchants (casados) without formal Crown fortresses
They were directly governed by the Bishop of Goa
They prohibited any trade of saltpetre or muslin
They were captured by the Ottoman navy in 1536
mockTestQuestions.sol: Bengal trade was decentralized and managed by private married settlers (casados) rather than the official Crown monopoly.

mockTestQuestions.q: How did Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat die in February 1537?
opts: He drowned in Diu harbor during a scuffle aboard the Governor's ship
He was executed in Lisbon for violating the treaty
He died of illness during the Siege of Diu
He was killed in a battle against Humayun at Ahmedabad
mockTestQuestions.sol: A violent scuffle during negotiations aboard da Cunha's vessel led to the Sultan falling into the harbor and drowning.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which Portuguese monarch ruled during the entire governorship of Nino da Cunha (1529–1538)?
mockTestQuestions.sol: King John III (João III) ruled Portugal from 1521 to 1557, overseeing the administration of Nino da Cunha.

mockTestQuestions.q: Where did Nino da Cunha die on his return voyage in 1539?
opts: At sea near the Cape of Good Hope
mockTestQuestions.sol: Nino da Cunha passed away at sea near the Cape of Good Hope.

mockTestQuestions.q: What was the land grant system implemented by the Portuguese in Bassein called?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Aforamento was the land grant system where lands were leased in exchange for quit-rents.
